articles.title: Hair Loss Linked to Aging Due to Smaller Hair Follicles
articles.summary: Hair loss after 50 is a common phenomenon, but it's not an inevitable part of aging. Many women experience changes in their hair as they approach this milestone age. According to...
articles.content: Hair loss after 50 is a common phenomenon, but it's not an inevitable part of aging. Many women experience changes in their hair as they approach this milestone age. According to trichologist Sharley Viola, these changes are linked to shifts in the hair growth cycle. As we age, our hair follicles gradually become smaller, leading to finer, shorter strands that lose pigment. This process is known as follicular miniaturization. The impact of aging on hair can be attributed to a combination of factors, including thyroid function and circulation. Biochemist Jared Reynolds notes that these underlying health issues can contribute to hair thinning. Hair care experts stress that it's essential to understand the root cause of hair loss before addressing it. A thorough examination of one's overall health can provide valuable insights into potential triggers for hair thinning. Declining thyroid activity with age can have a significant impact on hair growth and overall health. This decline can lead to thyroid imbalances that affect not just hair texture but also follicle health. In some cases, medications used to manage these imbalances can further exacerbate the issue. Reduced blood circulation within the scalp's microcirculatory system is another factor contributing to hair thinning in older individuals. As we age, this system becomes less efficient at supplying oxygen and nutrients to the hair follicles, which are essential for healthy growth. This reduction in circulation can be particularly problematic if left unaddressed. Hair loss prevention strategies often hinge on identifying its underlying causes, with some types being more preventable than others. For instance, hair thinning caused by age-related hormonal and follicular changes may not always be avoidable, but other factors such as thyroid imbalances or certain medications can be managed through medical treatment under a healthcare professional's guidance. Understanding the underlying causes of hair thinning after 50 is crucial in determining the most effective treatment approach. Medical professionals can help identify the root cause of hair loss and recommend personalized solutions. Topical treatments such as minoxidil have been shown to promote hair regrowth, according to Viola. However, styling products can also play a significant role in making thinning hair appear more voluminous. Sabina Wizemann, Director at the GH Beauty Personal Care Lab, advises against using heavy hair products that weigh down the hair. Instead, she recommends using volumizing mousses and root-lifting sprays to create lift and body throughout the lengths of fine and thinning hair. These styling options can help add volume without leaving the hair looking limp. For those who have tried topical treatments to no avail, there are in-office options available to stimulate hair growth. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) therapy involves scalp injections that can stimulate growth, while low-level laser therapy uses low-intensity light to encourage new hair development. A dermatologist should be consulted for these procedures. Reynolds emphasizes the importance of patience and consistency when trying to achieve desired results. It may take time to see noticeable improvements, but with a consistent routine, it is possible to achieve hair that boosts confidence. articles.title: Breakthrough in Bioprinting Technology Using Modified 3D Printer
articles.summary: A breakthrough in bioprinting technology has been announced by researchers at the University of Rochester, who have successfully modified a standard $450 3D printer to create living...
articles.content: A breakthrough in bioprinting technology has been announced by researchers at the University of Rochester, who have successfully modified a standard $450 3D printer to create living materials with over 100 layers. The team, led by Professor Anne S. Meyer, aimed to make DIY bioprinters affordable and accessible to scientists worldwide by using inexpensive parts that are easily obtainable. According to Meyer, the goal is to enable other researchers to create these bioprinters in their own labs without breaking the bank. The modified 3D printer replaces the plastic filament extruder with a syringe pump that dispenses bio-ink, a specialized formula combining living cells and a polymer solution. This unique mixture hardens into a gel once printed, setting it apart from traditional bioprinted materials. Using this low-cost setup, researchers can create living tissues with precise control over cell types and final shape. The possibilities are vast, ranging from cleaning up contaminated water to breaking down waste materials like plastic. The team's innovative approach addresses the significant drawback of current 3D bioprinters: their high cost and tendency to collapse before setting. The customized bioprinter's syringe is capable of both extrusion and retraction, preventing unwanted oozing at the edges of printed structures. This innovative setup allows for the creation of crisp shapes with well-defined edges, a significant improvement over previous DIY 3D bioprinters. The cost of this upgraded printer was remarkably low, thanks to its components being easily sourced from various suppliers. As a result, other labs can now build their own version of the printer and syringe pump. The new DIY bioprinter has expanded the possibilities for printing living structures by allowing for more than 100 layers. In contrast, previous versions were limited to fewer than 20 layers. This significant increase in complexity and height enables researchers to create hollow cavities within printed structures. The upgraded printer's capabilities open up new avenues for creating structures with a high surface-to-volume ratio. This allows embedded bacteria to efficiently receive signals or nutrients from their surroundings and excrete useful products at an accelerated rate. To facilitate the printing process, researchers developed a support gel called slurry that holds up bio-ink and helps it solidify quickly at any height. Two types of slurry were created: one for easy removal of the print and another designed for incubation that allows microbes in the bioprints to remain alive for four or more weeks. The versatility of this new slurry is vast, enabling researchers to create engineered biofilm materials that can mimic the characteristics of real-world biofilms or possess enhanced mechanical properties. Researchers can now test and study these artificially created biofilms in a controlled environment, gaining valuable insights into their behavior and interactions with surfaces. This breakthrough has significant implications for various fields, including medicine, where understanding biofilms is crucial for developing effective treatments. The creation of living materials with more than 100 layers using this modified $450 3D printer marks a major advancement in bioprinting technology, opening up new avenues for research and development in fields that rely on complex structures. articles.title: Walking After Meals Reduces Blood Sugar Levels
articles.summary: A recent study suggests that walking post-meal can boost metabolism and regulate blood sugar levels.
articles.content: A recent change in my evening routine has left me feeling more energized than ever, and it's all thanks to a simple yet effective habit - walking after every meal. Every night, as colleagues finish their dinner at a restaurant in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood, I slip out of the door for a brisk 10-minute walk home. This daily ritual began months ago when I stumbled upon a TikTok video from a nutritionist who claimed that short walks post-meal could boost metabolism and regulate blood sugar levels. The concept resonated with me, especially since I'm an avid walker and eater - two pastimes that are not mutually exclusive, as it turns out. According to internal medicine physician Elizabeth Sharp Edens, prolonged sitting after meals can lead to a higher post-meal blood-sugar response, but breaking it up with short walks can make a significant difference. Physician Elizabeth Sharp Edens explains that while brief periods of sitting after eating aren't inherently bad, prolonged inactivity can have negative consequences. My friend Elizabeth Sharp Edens, an internal medicine and obesity medicine physician, has shed some light on the topic. Research has shown that incorporating light-intensity walking into daily routines can have a significant impact on post-meal glucose levels. According to a 2022 meta-analysis published in Sports Medicine, walking after meals reduced glucose by nearly 17 percent. The science behind this phenomenon lies in the way muscles use glucose for energy when we walk. As Edens points out, our legs contain some of the largest muscles in the body, which makes sense given that walking stimulates muscle contractions that facilitate the movement of glucose transporters. This natural process can be a game-changer for those who struggle with feeling overly full or experiencing afternoon energy crashes. Rather than relying on supplements or peptides, walking offers an easy and free solution to improve digestion and prevent blood-sugar dips. Walking after meals can alleviate feelings of discomfort and fullness. According to research, a slow walk after a meal accelerates stomach emptying by reducing the time it takes for half its contents to be digested. This is particularly beneficial for individuals experiencing bloating, as mild walking has been shown to decrease intestinal gas retention from 45 percent to 24 percent and alleviate symptoms. Gravity also plays a role in digestion, notes Caitlin Hosmer, a registered dietitian based in Maine. She explains that walking can help mitigate uncomfortable fullness and reflux after meals due to the effects of gravity on digestion. Studies have demonstrated that even brief periods of walking can be effective in reducing post-meal glucose spikes. A 2025 study found that a 10-minute walk lowered glucose measurements by 6 percent, while a 30-minute walk resulted in a 5 percent decrease in glucose levels. Getting started on post-meal walks requires minimal effort and commitment. If you can manage just a short 10-minute stroll, it's better than nothing. In fact, even this brief period of movement has been shown to have a positive impact on glucose levels. The science behind why walking after meals is beneficial lies in the timing. According to Hosmer, glucose typically peaks within an hour or so after eating. By moving before this peak, individuals can effectively blunt the spike in glucose levels that often follows a meal. This simple yet effective strategy has been observed to yield significant results. Incorporating post-meal walks into daily routines may seem like a challenge, especially when time is of the essence. However, even brief intervals of 10 minutes have been found to make a difference. By prioritizing movement after meals, individuals can reap rewards that extend beyond improved digestion and energy levels. By incorporating post-meal walks into daily routines, individuals can experience a significant reduction in lethargy after eating. Feeling sluggish after meals is a common occurrence for many people, but by taking short walks, they can notice an improvement in their overall energy levels and digestion. Hosmer emphasizes that the goal of these walks isn't to push oneself to exhaustion, but rather to aid the body in processing the meal. articles.title: Groundbreaking Coral Diversity Discovery on Australia's East Coast
articles.summary: An international team of scientists has made a groundbreaking discovery on Australia's east coast, uncovering previously hidden coral diversity that sheds new light on the Great Barrier Reef.
articles.content: An international team of scientists has made a groundbreaking discovery on Australia's east coast, uncovering previously hidden coral diversity that sheds new light on the Great Barrier Reef. The research, led by Dr. Augustine Crosbie from James Cook University and Queensland Museum, focused on Acropora, one of the most diverse groups of reef-building corals, which includes branching staghorns and table-forming corals. A total of 53 named Acropora species were reassessed using cutting-edge genomic sequencing in combination with historical museum specimens. This comprehensive approach allowed researchers to reevaluate the distinctiveness of these coral species. The study found that 47 out of 53 Acropora species are supported as distinct, while four previously unresolved species have been recognized as valid. Furthermore, 12 species that were once considered variations of other species have been resurrected and given their own unique status. By connecting historical museum specimens with modern corals and genomic data, the researchers have gained a clearer understanding of coral diversity on the Great Barrier Reef. According to Dr. Crosbie, many of these corals had been known to science for over a century but were misinterpreted as variants of other coral species. For years, coral scientists have grappled with the issue of distinguishing between unique species and variations of existing ones based on physical characteristics. To address this challenge, researchers delved into museum collections worldwide, scrutinizing historical type specimens to gather valuable data. In many cases, these specimens consisted only of preserved skeletons, which couldn't be directly sequenced. To overcome this limitation, the team collected modern corals from locations where the species were first identified and linked them with genomic information. Recognizing distinct species is crucial for understanding and preserving coral biodiversity, according to Peter Cowman, principal scientist of marine biodiversity at Queensland Museum. Cowman emphasized that a seemingly common coral could actually comprise several species, each occupying a smaller geographic area. This insight has significant implications for assessing extinction risk and allocating conservation resources. The study of the Great Barrier Reef has been ongoing for decades, but researchers have now revealed that there is still much to be learned about this ecosystem. Despite being one of the most well-studied ecosystems on the planet, scientists have discovered that they have significantly underestimated the number of coral species living in the reef. This realization highlights the complexity and richness of the reef's biodiversity, emphasizing the importance of continued research and monitoring efforts. The findings underscore the need for a more nuanced understanding of the reef's ecosystem, with accurate knowledge of its constituent species being essential for effective conservation and protection strategies. articles.title: European Union Sending Team to Ukraine Conflict Talks
articles.summary: A team of diplomats from the European Union and several individual countries is being sent to negotiations on the Ukraine conflict.
articles.content: The European Union is sending a team of diplomats from the bloc and five individual countries to the next round of talks on the Ukraine conflict. The move comes after a summit focused on how to avoid being shut out of US-led negotiations aimed at ending the nearly five-year war. European Council President Antonio Costa announced that the continent will be represented by officials from the 27-nation EU block, as well as from France, Germany, Italy, Poland, and the UK. These countries have formed a "Coalition of the Willing to support Ukraine in its conflict with Russia. We need to integrate all of us," Costa said, "and for this it's essential to have a team and to speak with only one voice." This statement reflects concerns among European leaders that they may be left on the sidelines as US-backed negotiations unfold. Ukraine is eager for its European allies' support in these talks. The country has expressed reluctance to leave the negotiations solely in the hands of the US administration, which some have perceived as leaning towards Moscow's views. European leaders are wary of leaving negotiations over Ukraine solely in the hands of the US administration, which they perceive as having a leaning towards Moscow's views. French President Emmanuel Macron emphasized the importance of European involvement in the talks, stating that "Without Europeans, there is no support for Ukraine" and "There is no more US support". This sentiment was echoed by Macron at a meeting of the European Political Community in Dublin, where he noted that Europe will ultimately define its own future security. European leaders are concerned that Russian President Vladimir Putin may use his influence over Trump to secure a peace settlement that weakens not just Ukraine but also broader European security. As envoys from Washington, Moscow, and Kyiv met in Abu Dhabi, several European countries attended discussions nearby, including the UK, France, and Germany. The European Union's representation at the negotiating table has been a contentious issue in recent weeks. A unified voice for the EU would provide clarity and consistency in its interactions with other nations. Critics argue that without a single representative, individual countries or small groups may engage in diplomatic efforts that do not align with the EU's overall stance. This fragmented approach can lead to confusion and undermine the EU's negotiating power. Some European leaders have advocated for a single envoy to represent the EU at these talks. However, this proposal has been met with resistance from others who believe a team-based approach would be more effective in conveying the complexity of EU interests. The question of who represents Europe is further complicated by the EU's loose definition and its multiple overlapping structures, including the 27-nation EU, NATO, and the Schengen zone. The EU's decision to send a team to represent its interests in Ukraine talks has been made possible by the choice of a collective representation over an individual envoy. This approach allows for participation from nations that have pledged military support for a future ceasefire as part of the "coalition of the willing", including the UK which left the EU in 2020. Poland is playing a significant role in these talks, speaking up for countries on the eastern flank that face constant threats from Russia's influence campaigns and disruptive drones. The representation of the EU's institutions remains unclear, with speculation surrounding potential candidates including Costa and Kaja Kallas, the EU's top diplomat. Kallas has laid claim to the envoy role, saying she is representing Europe in foreign and security policy, but others are not so optimistic about the prospects for success. European leaders are bracing for a potentially awkward encounter between Trump and Putin in Beijing, fearing another unexpected development like the Alaska summit where Ukrainian and European representatives were notably absent. The absence of Ukraine's voice has left many concerned that Europe's interests may be overlooked once again, prompting calls from some leaders to maintain unity and coordination with Ukraine. articles.title: Japanese Knives Outperform Western Counterparts in Kitchen Tests
articles.summary: A range of Japanese-style knives have been thoroughly reviewed for their utility and effectiveness, providing insight into their suitability for various cooking tasks.
articles.content: The market for Japanese knives has seen a significant surge in recent years, outperforming their Western counterparts in various kitchen tests. Western-style knives are often larger and more versatile, having been used by chefs as makeshift tools for tasks such as opening cans of tomatoes during service. In contrast, Japanese knives prioritize precision cuts and typically serve a specific purpose, making them ideal for particular cooking tasks. The specificity of Japanese knives can make it challenging to determine which ones are necessary for a kitchen, but fortunately, extensive testing has been conducted on various models. A range of Japanese-style knives will be covered in this series, including the Gyuto, Santoku, Nakiri, Deba, Petty, Funayuki, and Kiritsuke, as well as the Honesuki. These knives have been thoroughly reviewed to provide insight into their utility and effectiveness, giving readers confidence in their purchasing decisions. The gyuto's design allows it to excel at slicing meat due to its curved edge, but its straighter blade also makes it suitable for chopping herbs. Compared to Western chef's knives, the gyuto has a lower profile and a drop point tip, making it easier to maneuver in tight spaces. The gyuto's sharp edge and thin blade enable precise slicing, allowing users to place the knife's tip on the cutting board and draw it through food with ease. Many home cooks prefer the gyuto as their daily driver due to its versatility and effectiveness, often opting for it over traditional chef's knives. A fan favorite among our team is MAC's Professional Hollow Ground Chef's Knife, which has topped our chef's knife reviews for years. The Kazan Arare by Shibata gyuto offers a more traditional take on the gyuto design, with a wicked sharp blade that impressed us enough to warrant its own review. A santoku knife's versatility makes it ideal for everyday tasks such as slicing cheese and an apple or chopping vegetables for a curry. The length of a santoku typically ranges between six to seven inches, which contrasts with the longer gyuto design often seen in Japanese knives. Our top pick among santoku models is the MAC Professional Santoku Knife, but we also recommend the Kazan Ginsan Nashiji Santoku for its razor-sharp blade and traditional wa-style handle. Nakiri knives are designed specifically for chopping vegetables and feature a straight edge and sturdy spine that allows for efficient push cuts. The nakiri's unique design makes it perfect for tasks such as matchsticking carrots or breaking down tough-skinned squash, and its heavier build also lends itself to more demanding cutting tasks. Deba knives are designed not just for chopping but also for precision slicing, typically featuring a single-bevel edge that allows for finer points than double-bevel edges. This unique design enables deba knives to portion out delicate fish fillets with ease, thanks in part to the sheep's foot tip which adds to their cutting prowess. The single-bevel edge is a defining feature of deba knives and sets them apart from other types of blades. While we haven't had the opportunity to test deba knives ourselves, as they do require some knowledge and skill to use effectively for breaking down whole fish, there are options available for those interested in trying one out. The Seki Mago Roku Deba from Kai is a solid choice, offering an affordable entry point into the world of deba knives. However, we would caution most people against choosing a deba knife as their first purchase, instead recommending nakiri or santoku knives which offer more versatility and ease of use in everyday kitchen tasks. These types of knives are better suited to the needs of most cooks. The petty knife is another option worth considering, named for its diminutive size - "petite being French for small. This tiny blade, typically around five inches long, is a miniature version of the popular gyuto knife. Petty knives make excellent utility blades for tackling small tasks such as dicing shallots or slicing herbs, and their length also makes them suitable for slicing larger items like steaks - provided you don't rely on handheld turning and peeling. We've found that certain models, including the MAC Professional Petty Knife and the Tojiro Classic Petty Knife, strike a perfect balance between sharpness and size. The funayuki is an old-school Japanese knife shape that has been around for centuries, likely influencing the design of other popular knives such as the gyuto and santoku. This traditional knife has a distinctive shorter length, typically around seven inches long, with a narrow pointed tip and a tall heel. Its compact size makes it perfect for precision cuts in tight spaces. Its shape is often described as a combination of the santoku's width and the gyuto's curved blade, resulting in a unique utility knife that can handle various tasks in the kitchen. Unlike the deba knife, which was used for fish butchery due to its heavy single-bevel design, the funayuki is designed to be lightweight and agile. This makes it ideal for fishermen who need to fillet their catch on the boat. Today, home cooks might choose a funayuki as a secondary gyuto or opt for this shape over a santoku as an all-purpose utility knife with a narrower tip. The Akiru-Saku Funayuki Gyuto is a modern take on the traditional funayuki design, featuring a more angular sword tip that allows for precise cuts. A Japanese slicing knife known as the kiritsuke combines elements of both long and short knives. Its unique shape includes an angular sword tip" and a tall heel, making it similar to the santoku in design. When reviewing chef's knives, we found that the Shun Classic Kiritsuke was an excellent all-purpose chef's knife with a distinctive tip curve upwards more like Western-style knives, allowing for a rock chop motion. The Japanese honesuki is a specialized boning knife shape designed for poultry, but its unique design makes it surprisingly versatile. A steep, wedge-shaped knife with a very fine point and tall heel, the honesuki's goal is to delicately slip between chicken joints while cutting through cartilage. This versatility extends beyond its original purpose, making it suitable for small chopping and dicing tasks that would normally require a petty knife. In particular, the honesuki shape outperforms curved fillet knives in these utility tasks, showcasing its adaptability. The MAC Professional Honesuki is an excellent option to consider, offering a balance of sharpness and versatility for both boning-knife duties and general utility work. This nonconventional multitasker can be a valuable addition to any kitchen, especially for those who frequently break down whole chickens while also needing a knife for tasks like slicing strawberries. articles.title: Study Finds No Benefit from Common Classroom Accommodations for Students with ADHD
articles.summary: A new study has found that common classroom accommodations for children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) do not improve their behavior or academic performance.
articles.content: A new study from Florida International University has raised questions about the effectiveness of common classroom accommodations for students with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Researchers evaluated four widely used approaches to see if they actually help children succeed. The accommodations examined included extra time on assignments, regular breaks, working at a standing desk, and studying in a quiet area. However, none of these strategies showed significant improvements in classroom behavior or academic performance among the 255 children with ADHD involved in the study. According to Gregory Fabiano, professor of psychology at FIU and lead author of the research, there was no evidence that any of the accommodations worked even when combined with other treatments like behavioral interventions or medication. This finding may come as a surprise given the widespread use of these accommodations in schools. The study involved children with ADHD who participated in FIU's Summer Treatment Program between 2022 and 2025. The program aimed to provide a supportive environment for kids with ADHD to learn and develop skills. Further research is needed to determine what types of accommodations might be more effective in helping students with ADHD succeed. Researchers conducted an experiment to measure the effectiveness of various classroom accommodations in helping students with ADHD succeed academically. While some common classroom accommodations showed no significant benefits, other interventions had a measurable impact on student behavior and academic performance. Behavioral treatments were found to have a particularly positive effect, reducing rule violations during independent work by 37%. This reduction was significantly higher than the decrease seen when children received neither treatment nor medication. Stimulant medication also proved effective in reducing rule violations, with a notable decrease of 61% compared to children who received no treatment. Furthermore, medication helped students complete more work and earn higher quiz scores, indicating an improvement in academic performance. The results suggest that certain interventions can have a tangible impact on student behavior and learning. Many classroom accommodations are designed to address specific ADHD symptoms, such as difficulty paying attention or staying seated. However, these accommodations may not necessarily address the underlying challenges that interfere with a child's ability to learn and complete schoolwork. The assumption that common ADHD accommodations are effective for all students may be misguided, according to researchers who warn against a "one-size-fits-all" approach. Fabiano highlights that while some children may benefit from specific supports tailored to their needs, a blanket application of accommodations is unlikely to yield the desired results. Instead, he advocates for a more nuanced understanding of ADHD and its effects on individual students. Positive behavioral supports are gaining traction as an effective way to help children with ADHD stay motivated and focused in class. Fabiano recommends that teachers incorporate simple strategies such as praising good behavior, setting clear expectations, and providing consistent feedback into their everyday routines. Daily report cards can also be a valuable tool for establishing individual goals and tracking progress. By receiving regular feedback and positive reinforcement for meeting their targets, children with ADHD are more likely to stay on track and meet the expectations set by their teachers. Teachers are being encouraged to rethink their approach when it comes to helping students with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) succeed in the classroom. Instead of just providing more time for assignments, they should focus on setting specific goals and regularly checking in on progress. This shift in strategy is aimed at strengthening behaviors that support learning, rather than simply modifying the environment around a student. By doing so, teachers can help children with ADHD develop essential skills and habits that will benefit them throughout their academic careers. The study's findings have also sparked questions about the use of common accommodations in individualized education programs (IEPs) and Section 504 plans. These documents are designed to meet each child's unique needs, but it appears they may not be as effective as previously thought. Schools should prioritize behavioral interventions in general education classrooms, where most children with ADHD spend their school day. This includes students who receive special education services, and parents can play a key role in ensuring their child's IEP or 504 plan is tailored to their individual needs. Pelham's research has significantly altered our understanding of ADHD treatment approaches. While stimulant medication may improve classroom behavior and productivity in children, it does not necessarily enhance their ability to absorb new information. This discrepancy was discovered by Pelham and his team in a 2022 study that aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of various treatments for ADHD. The findings suggest that medication alone is insufficient to address the complex needs of children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. In contrast, starting with behavioral interventions has been found to be more cost-effective than initiating treatment with medication. This approach was identified by Pelham's earlier work as a viable option for improving outcomes in children with ADHD. The research underscores the importance of considering multiple factors when developing effective treatments for this condition. It also highlights the need for further investigation into the most suitable approaches. According to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, approximately 7.1 million children in the United States have a current ADHD diagnosis. This accounts for nearly 12% of those aged 3 to 17 who receive an ADHD diagnosis each year. Many of these children rely on Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) and Section 504 plans to access additional support at school. The study suggests that classroom accommodations for students with ADHD may not be enough to ensure their success. While these students rely heavily on Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) and Section 504 plans, it seems that a more comprehensive approach is needed to support them effectively. The emphasis should shift from relying solely on accommodations to implementing effective treatments within the regular classroom environment. By giving children with ADHD the best chance to succeed, educators can help them feel proud of their accomplishments in the classroom. articles.title: American Airlines Overhauls LAX Route Map with Nine Impacted Routes
articles.summary: The airline is making changes to several routes, including resuming seasonal regional service from Los Angeles to Grand Junction, Colorado.
articles.content: American Airlines has unveiled a major overhaul of its Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) route map, with nine routes impacted by the changes. The carrier made the announcement just minutes after rumors surfaced that it was planning to reveal new routes at LAX. The news will be welcomed by some AA flyers in Southern California who have been eagerly awaiting the return of service to certain destinations. One of the most significant developments is the resumption of seasonal regional service from LAX to Grand Junction, Colorado. After a five-year hiatus, American Airlines will once again offer flights between Los Angeles and Grand Junction Regional Airport (GJT) using a Bombardier CRJ700 aircraft. The route will operate from May 27 to August 9, replacing the carrier's existing service to Aspen/Pitkin County Airport (ASE), which will be closed for construction in 2027. As part of its ongoing efforts to revamp its Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) operations, American Airlines is introducing changes to several routes. One notable adjustment involves the airline's service from LAX to Grand Junction Regional Airport (GJT), which will now be operated using one of its smaller CRJ-700 aircraft. On a more positive note, American is increasing regular service on two previously seasonal routes: Reno, Nevada, and Bozeman, Montana. The former will see year-round flights three times daily starting May 27, while the latter's seasonal return will take place from May 27 to August 9. Both routes will be serviced by an Embraer 175 regional jet. In addition to these changes, American is boosting frequencies on several other routes from LAX. Denver, Las Vegas, and Seattle will all receive more flights, with the exact schedule to be determined. Furthermore, the airline's transcontinental service from LA to Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD) is being enhanced with twice-daily departures starting in May. This increased frequency will enable American to better compete with its cross-country Los Angeles service from nearby Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA), which has been a strong performer for the carrier. The strengthened IAD-LAX routes are expected to provide passengers with more convenient travel options and improved connectivity. However, not all changes at LAX are positive. American is cutting ties with two routes: Cleveland Hopkins International Airport (CLE) and Des Moines, Iowa, both of which will cease operations on February 11. This network revamp in LA marks a significant shift for the carrier as it rethinks its route offerings at its Southern California hub. American Airlines' Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) service is undergoing a significant transformation as the carrier reworks its route offerings in Southern California. articles.title: Aranui Cruises Offers Freight and Passenger Service to Marquesas Islands
articles.summary: Passengers can explore remote islands in French Polynesia while cargo is unloaded from ships.
articles.content: The allure of hopping a freighter and sailing to the distant South Pacific has long been a romantic notion for many. The prospect of spending days at sea gazing out at seabirds and cargo pallets is a siren's call to adventure-seekers. In this tranquil setting, passengers can wake up to the sounds of cargo being offloaded onto tiny concrete wharfs, where they'll meet the local community nestled among swaying palm trees. Alternatively, they could take the day to hike or tour the island, or indulge in a feast of fresh catches with the locals while watching the unloading process. The Aranui Cruises company has been offering dedicated cruises built around this premise for over 40 years. Based in French Polynesia, the locally owned cruise line operates combination passenger and cargo services from Papeete, Tahiti, to the dramatically rugged volcanic landscapes of the Marquesas Islands. Aranui's ships operate a cargo service to remote islands that have no airport and are only accessible by sea, two of them being Fatu Hiva and Tahuata. While the ship is unloading its cargo of soft drinks, groceries, building supplies, and even racing canoes in the port, passengers can use their time to explore the surrounding area. In March 2026, I boarded the purpose-built Aranui V for a 12-night journey to the Marquesas Islands. The Aranui V's cargo hold is a stark contrast to its luxurious cruise section, but for me, that unique combination was part of the appeal. Dr. Carole S. Ivory's lectures on Marquesan culture and art were a highlight of my days onboard, providing valuable context for the experiences we had ashore. The ship's included shore excursions allowed us to immerse ourselves in the local culture, visiting archaeological sites and volcanic formations with expert guides who knew every nook and cranny. On Nuku Hiva, our group explored by car, while on other islands, organized hikes gave us a chance to take in the breathtaking scenery at our own pace. Optional excursions offered additional opportunities for exploration, like the scenic drive between villages on Fatu Hiva, which came with an unforgettable sunset barge ride back to the ship. The local cuisine on board Aranui V was a highlight for passengers, with dishes such as chow mein from the snack bar at the botanical garden offering a taste of the islands' unique flavors. Fresh produce and meats were also showcased in the buffet, where island specialties like coconut milk-roasted goat, poisson cru (raw fish salad), steamed taro, rice, and magenta-colored mashed banana swimming in sweet condensed coconut milk were served up. Community gatherings were an integral part of each port stop, with local musicians and artisans performing at community pavilions on various islands visited by the Aranui V. Skilled carvers from the Marquesas Islands showcased their expertise in crafting intricately decorated bowls, canoe paddles, jewelry, and other items using wood, bone, and a unique volcanic rock called te ke'a pua (flower stone). The vibrant colors and natural patterns found in this polished rock were particularly striking when crafted into ornamental fish hooks, decorative whales and birds, or pestles used to smash taro. The crew of Aranui were familiar faces for me, having sailed together on another island group four years prior. This familiarity extended beyond just recognition - passengers and crew alike can freely mingle on board, unlike on other ships where separation is more strictly enforced. Evenings often blur the lines between work and leisure as many crew members join passengers in the bar for post-dinner drinks. In my previous experience sailing with Aranui to the Austral Islands, I had a chance encounter with the head of housekeeping who showcased her poker skills by cleaning out the ship's captain during an impromptu game in the pearl boutique. Onboard amenities extend beyond just entertainment - when I suffered a broken sandal on landing craft duty at Ua Huka, staff directed me to the ship's French doctor for a quick repair. The farewell ceremony to the Marquesas Islands was a poignant moment for all passengers as we gathered on the deck of Aranui V. The island's rich culture and breathtaking landscapes had left an indelible mark on our hearts. A member of the onboard staff led us in a prayer of gratitude, thanking the islands for their hospitality and sharing some final words of farewell. In a symbolic gesture, we tossed armfuls of local flowers and plants into the sea as they caught the last rays of sunlight. The experience had a lasting impact on me, evoking vivid memories long after my return home, the scent of straw hats, the taste of baked bananas, and the vibrant colors of the islands' flora and fauna still lingered in my mind. articles.content: The Commerce Department is facing growing pressure from its fellow Cabinet members over Secretary Howard Lutnick's decision not to blacklist Megaspeed, a cloud computing company at the center of a high-profile scandal involving Nvidia and an alleged Chinese spy. According to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, there was significant coordination among federal agencies in favor of placing trade restrictions on Megaspeed for months. However, the final decision ultimately rested with Lutnick's department. Bessent made these remarks during a recent interview, noting that Commerce has the authority to make such decisions. When asked about his own role in the process, Bessent suggested that he was not responsible for determining which entities should be placed on the entity list. Megaspeed is currently under investigation by the Justice Department over allegations that it violated U.S. export controls by shipping Nvidia chips to China. The company's Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatric, shipped at least $7.5 billion in chips to China over a two-year period. Reports have also emerged suggesting that Lutnick took action to protect Nvidia from the Trump administration's export controls on U.S.-made AI hardware destined for China. Bessent was reportedly so concerned about this development that he confronted Lutnick in the Situation Room following the midterm elections, according to Axios. The controversy surrounding Nvidia's advanced AI chips continues to grow as senior White House officials consider ousting Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick from his position. This move comes after it was revealed that Lutnick failed to add 100 companies, including China's DeekSeek, to the entity list despite being given months to do so by Treasury officials. According to reports, Lutnick's top deputy Jeff Kessler spoke out against cancelling a $7 billion deal with Oracle to lease chips to Chinese tech conglomerate Tencent. This decision would have halted the shipment of 100,000 advanced Nvidia AI chips, and Lutnick was reportedly at odds with Treasury officials over the cancellation. The Commerce Department has yet to respond to Fortune's request for comment on this matter. Meanwhile, lawmakers from both parties are calling for accountability from Lutnick, questioning why he chose to sell advanced chips despite national security concerns. Lutnick is set to testify alongside Huang before the Senate Banking Committee on December 10 to address these concerns. The fallout from Nvidia's involvement with Megaspeed and its ties to China continues to widen, with senior White House officials weighing whether to remove Lutnick from his position as Commerce Secretary. Senior officials within the Treasury Department had been pushing for months to blacklist Megaspeed, a US-based chipmaker accused of ties to China, citing concerns about favoritism toward Nvidia, a major tech company. The Commerce Secretary's close relationship with Nvidia and his financial ties to the company have raised eyebrows, particularly given his position as chief regulator. Huang, who has praised Lutnick's industry expertise, had described him as a key contact within the administration. articles.title: Anna Sui draws inspiration from films like Performance and Love and Anarchy
articles.summary: The designer's love of vintage fashion and 1970s cinema is reflected in her designs that blend nostalgic elements with modern twists.
articles.content: Anna Sui's eponymous brand has always been built on a deep respect for the past. This reverence is reflected in her designs, which expertly blend niche references from different eras to create a distinctly modern aesthetic. Industry insiders have long recognized the connection between style and intellect. Our new series, The Well-Dressed Mind, explores this intersection by asking tastemakers and professionals in the industry for their cultural recommendations. Recently, we asked Anna Sui, a downtown New York designer of her generation, about the films that inspire her work. Sui's love of vintage fashion, design, photography, and art is the foundation of her brand. As one of the defining designers of her era, she has always drawn on these influences to create clothes that feel both nostalgic and forward-thinking. Anna Sui's fascination with 1970s cinema continues to influence her designs. The film Performance, directed by Donald Cammell and Nicolas Roeg, is a standout example of this inspiration. Set in London, it tells the story of a gangster struggling with his identity crisis while hiding at the home of a rock star, played by Mick Jagger, who lives with two girlfriends. One of those girlfriends, Anita Pallenberg, was a style icon of her time and has likely had an impact on Sui's aesthetic. The film's themes of identity and rebellion are also echoed in Sui's designs, which often blend nostalgic elements with modern twists. Her ability to balance these opposing forces is a key part of what makes her clothes so appealing. Sui's love of 1970s cinema doesn't stop at Performance, however. She has also cited Lina Wertmüller's Love and Anarchy as an influence, a film set in a brothel in fascist Italy during the 1930s. The film's themes of rebellion and nonconformity are likely to have resonated with Sui, who often incorporates elements of counterculture into her designs. The 1972 film Cabaret had a significant impact on Anna Sui's aesthetic, particularly in its portrayal of the Kit Kat Club and 1930s Weimar Republic Germany. The movie features an incredible cast, including Joel Grey, Michael York, and Marisa Berenson, who all bring to life the decadent atmosphere of the era. The film's costumes, designed by Bob Fosse and Shirley Russell, are particularly noteworthy, with Liza Minnelli's iconic looks being a major influence on Sui. Minnelli's character Sally Bowles is a dynamic figure, and her style has stayed with Anna Sui forever. articles.summary: Nithya Raman made her first public appearance as Los Angeles Mayor-Elect in a bold outfit that sent a message about her style and personality, featuring a vintage tangerine Narciso Rodriguez motorcycle jacket paired with Eckhaus Latta jeans.
articles.content: Nithya Raman made her first public appearance as Los Angeles Mayor-Elect in a bold outfit that sent a message about her style and personality. The vintage tangerine Narciso Rodriguez motorcycle jacket was a striking choice, paired with a pair of Eckhaus Latta jeans that caught the attention of onlookers. Raman's fashion evolution is notable, given her background as a two-term LA councilmember who often adhered to traditional attire in her official appearances. She would typically wear button-down shirts and matching pantsuits, conforming to the expectations of her role. The transformation in Raman's style can be attributed to a trio of unlikely advisors: Zoe Latta, a fashion designer from Eckhaus Latta, and celebrity stylists Kat Typaldos and Turner. They have been instrumental in helping Raman break free from conventional fashion norms for politicians. Female politicians often face restrictions when it comes to their wardrobe choices, with silhouettes being heavily influenced by traditional styles that can come across as overly conservative. Even small additions, such as a pussy bow blouse, may not be enough to deviate from these expectations. As Nithya Raman navigated the early days of her surprise bid for Los Angeles mayor, her wardrobe didn't receive much attention from her campaign team. Instead of focusing on fashion, Raman wore a uniform of sorts - "a lot of capes that Latta affectionately described, which suited her traditional approach to politics. Raman's decision not to prioritize her wardrobe was likely due in part to the numerous demands on her time and energy during this period. The styling team's approach was guided by a simple yet effective principle: dressing Nithya Raman for her mayoral campaign required a subtle and sustainable touch. Vintage and secondhand pieces from The RealReal were carefully blended with local designers' creations to reflect the candidate's understated style, while also appealing to the sensibilities of the team as small business owners. Their focus was on creating outfits that would resonate with Raman's constituents, rather than showcasing high-end fashion. This meant incorporating items that could easily be incorporated into a workwear wardrobe. I'm thinking about [the client], the context, the world that they live in, Turner emphasizes, highlighting the importance of considering the individual and their environment when styling. Stylists Zoe Latta, Kat Typaldos, and Turner worked closely with Nithya Raman to help her develop a sense of personal style. Typaldos recalls that Raman was very particular about what she wore, often opting for denim as a staple in her wardrobe. This attention to detail is a testament to the politician's agency when it comes to fashion choices. articles.title: Disney and Meta Launch 3D Content on Quest 3 and 3S Headsets
articles.summary: The arrival of 3D content on VR headsets marks a significant shift in home entertainment.
articles.content: Disney and Meta have finally brought a new level of immersion to home entertainment with the launch of 3D content on the Quest 3 and 3S headsets. This development marks a significant shift in the way consumers can experience high-definition 3D movies from the comfort of their own homes. The arrival of 3D movies on VR headsets is particularly notable given the decline of 3D TVs, which once promised to revolutionize home entertainment but ultimately failed to gain widespread traction. However, with the rise of virtual reality technology, it seems that 3D content has found a new lease on life. Meta's Quest 3 and 3S headsets have been equipped with a library of 3D films, including some classic titles like Moana and Zootopia, which are now available to stream from within the Disney+ app. The company's decision to include 3D content in its latest headsets is a welcome move for fans of immersive entertainment. The experience of watching 3D movies on these headsets has been met with excitement, but it also raises questions about why Meta took so long to introduce this feature and why the Quest 2 was left out of the loop. The company's operating system may be constraining the potential of 3D content on its headsets. The integration of 3D movies into the Disney+ app is a significant development, but it also highlights the limitations of Meta's current technology. As more users explore the possibilities of VR entertainment, it will be interesting to see how these platforms evolve and improve over time. Disney has finally made its vast library of 3D films available to Disney+ subscribers, including popular titles from Marvel, Pixar, and Star Wars franchises. Users can simply select a movie, verify that it supports 3D viewing, and start watching on their Meta Quest 3 headset. The visual experience is nothing short of impressive, with a heightened sense of depth that outshines traditional 2D screens. The opening scenes of Guardians of the Galaxy and the high-octane car chase from Black Panther are just two examples of how Disney's 3D library shines on the Quest 3. One major advantage of watching 3D movies on VR headsets is their ability to produce brighter, more vivid visuals compared to dimly lit cinema screens. This phenomenon remains true even with the Quest 3, making it an ideal platform for experiencing immersive 3D content. However, users are advised to invest in a good pair of headphones when watching these 3D movies on the Quest 3, as its built-in speakers lack depth and low-end impact. The headset does support advanced audio features like Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, but their effects are somewhat diminished by the device's limitations. The Quest 3's LCD screens do not support true HDR, which may be a drawback for some viewers. Nevertheless, Disney's extensive library of 3D movies is now accessible to subscribers, making it an exciting development in the world of VR entertainment. Meta's Horizon OS has undergone significant changes to mirror the design language of Apple's visionOS. However, when it comes to media playback, the flexibility is lacking. Users cannot easily resize the Disney+ window on their Quest 3 headset, forcing them to place it within a specific area designated by Meta. For those who crave an immersive cinematic experience, playing 3D videos within the cinema environment provides a makeshift solution. This allows users to sit in various positions and enjoy a more expansive field of view, although it's not ideal for multitasking with other VR apps. The compromise is necessary due to the limitations imposed by Meta's OS design. The delayed introduction of 3D movies on the Quest 3 has left many wondering what took Meta so long. The company had ample time to implement this feature, especially considering that there were no technical barriers preventing it from doing so. Apple's Vision Pro might have been a factor in Disney+ content exclusivity, but it didn't hinder Meta's ability to offer 3D films. The availability of 3D movies is now accessible on the Quest 3, courtesy of Disney's extensive library. However, this development comes at a time when Quest sales are dwindling, rendering it less of a selling point for potential buyers. The delay has sparked curiosity about what could have been if Meta had acted sooner. As users navigate through their VR content, they can now enjoy Disney's 3D movies within the confines of the cinema environment or as separate windows. Nevertheless, this solution does not address the underlying limitations of Meta's OS, which restricts users' ability to customize their viewing experience. The introduction of high-quality 3D movies to Meta's Quest 3 and 3S headsets has been met with enthusiasm from users who can now enjoy immersive entertainment without the need for expensive VR glasses. The delayed availability of this feature is likely due to the company's desire to reserve it as a selling point for its upcoming premium product. The fact that high-quality 3D movies are now available on Meta's Quest headsets provides a welcome respite from the limitations of the device, but does not address the underlying restrictions that prevent users from customizing their viewing experience. Nevertheless, this development offers users with existing Quest headsets a much-needed upgrade to their entertainment options. articles.title: Robert Louis Stevenson's First Draft of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde Destroyed
articles.summary: A previously unknown letter from Fanny Stevenson has shed new light on the mysterious destruction of Robert Louis Stevenson's first draft of "Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde".
articles.content: Robert Louis Stevenson's household in Bournemouth, England was a scene of great turmoil in the autumn of 1885. The author was confined to bed for much of his time due to illness and financial strain, struggling to make ends meet. His wife Fanny Stevenson often had to intervene when her husband would cry out in distress during his sleep. One such episode occurred on a particular night when he suddenly sat up and exclaimed that he was dreaming a fine bogey tale. The experience seemed to have a profound effect on Robert Louis Stevenson, as he began writing down the story by daybreak. Over the next three days, he produced a first draft of what would eventually become Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde. Fanny Stevenson witnessed her husband's feverish creativity firsthand, but she had no idea that this early draft was soon to meet its demise. The manuscript was burned in the fireplace, leaving behind only fragments of what once existed. The exact circumstances surrounding the destruction of the first draft are still shrouded in mystery. However, there exist multiple accounts from eyewitnesses who attempted to recount the events, each with their own version of how it happened. Despite the loss of the original manuscript, Robert Louis Stevenson's perseverance paid off as he went on to produce one of his most enduring works. But what exactly led to the destruction of that first draft remains a tale worth exploring further in this story. A previously unknown letter from Fanny Stevenson to her friend W.E. Henley surfaced ahead of an auction at Phillips in London, shedding new light on the mysterious first draft of Robert Louis Stevenson's "Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde. The letter, which made headlines in October 2000, revealed that Fanny had dismissed the draft as worthless, saying it was a quire full of utter nonsense. Fanny's scathing assessment of her husband's work came despite his claims that it was his greatest achievement. She even went so far as to threaten to burn the draft after showing it to Henley, indicating a deep-seated frustration with Stevenson's writing. The auction house had estimated the letter would sell for around £1,500, but its contents were of greater interest than its monetary value. Liz Merry, head of Phillips' book department, speculated that Fanny may have been put off by the themes of duality and darkness in Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde. However, Fanny's concerns went beyond mere aesthetics. In an earlier letter quoted by The Guardian, she expressed her fear that Stevenson was wasting his energy on a story that would never amount to anything. Fanny's anxieties were not unfounded, given the couple's financial struggles. They were deeply in debt, and Stevenson's writing career had yet to yield significant returns. Fanny's words suggest that she saw her husband's obsession with Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde as a luxury they could ill afford. The letter raises more questions than it answers about the fate of the first draft. What exactly led to its destruction remains a mystery, and one that continues to fascinate literary scholars and enthusiasts alike. The auction house's book department head, Liz Merry, has offered a theory about Fanny Stevenson's motivations for destroying her husband's first draft of 'Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde'. According to Merry, Fanny may have found the story's theme of duality distasteful, suggesting that she was uneasy with Robert Louis Stevenson's writing for a popular shilling shocker market. Fanny had valid reasons to worry about her husband's writing beyond personal taste. The couple was deeply in debt, and it seems likely that Fanny saw his literary endeavors as a costly distraction from their financial troubles. In an earlier letter quoted by a reputable publication, she expressed concern that Stevenson's latest work would be energy wasted, echoing the failure of his previous projects. In a preface written for a 1905 edition of her husband's collected works, Fanny shared a different account of the destroyed first draft. According to this version, the initial thirty-thousand-word manuscript was completed in just three days but ultimately deemed unsatisfactory due to its failure to convey the allegory that would become the heart of 'Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde'. Fanny attributed the draft's shortcomings to haste and the influence of a dream, suggesting that her husband had been driven by an external force rather than his own creative vision. While this explanation may seem vague, it highlights the complex interplay between Stevenson's artistic impulses and the pressures he faced in his personal life. Fanny's account raises more questions than answers about the destruction of the first draft. Who was responsible for its demise? Was Fanny herself involved, or did she simply acquiesce to her husband's decision to start anew? The mystery surrounding this pivotal moment in literary history continues to fascinate scholars and enthusiasts alike. The debate over the destroyed draft is further complicated by Fanny's ambiguous portrayal of events. While she does not directly implicate herself in the destruction, her account implies a level of involvement that leaves room for interpretation. As a result, readers are left to ponder the motivations behind this pivotal moment in literary history and its lasting impact on the development of 'Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde'. Lloyd Osbourne's account provides a vivid glimpse into Stevenson's creative process during that autumn at Skerryvore. Stevenson had been reading his draft aloud to Lloyd and his mother Fanny, who was not impressed by what she heard. She criticized the work, saying that Stevenson had missed the allegory" and made it "merely a story. This criticism clearly struck a nerve with Stevenson, as he became furious. Lloyd Osbourne chose to leave the room rather than continue listening to the argument between his stepfather and mother. However, when he returned to the scene, Stevenson was already coming downstairs, having apparently conceded Fanny's point. Stevenson's concession was followed by a dramatic gesture: he took the manuscript of his draft and threw it into the fire. This act was not entirely unopposed, as Fanny made an attempt to prevent him from doing so, but her efforts were ultimately unsuccessful. Fanny's son Lloyd later recalled Stevenson's statement when throwing away the manuscript: I have absolutely missed the allegory, which, after all, is the whole point of it. The debate surrounding the destruction of Stevenson's first draft of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde continues to this day, with multiple accounts from those present at the scene offering conflicting details. According to Lloyd, Stevenson explained his decision to destroy the manuscript by stating that it was all wrong", implying that he had lost sight of the story's central theme. This led him to conclude that the only way forward was to start anew and put temptation beyond his reach. The accounts of who actually destroyed the manuscript are unclear, with different versions placing blame on various individuals. Fanny recalled that Stevenson wrote the new version in just three days, while Lloyd estimated it took a bit longer. Despite their differences, all accounts agree on one thing: the first draft was gone for good. The second version, however, proved to be a resounding success, with Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde being published in 1886 to great acclaim. Fanny later noted that the book's popularity extended far beyond literary circles, with it being pirated across America and even used as a text for clergymen's sermons. Whatever was lost in the original draft remains a mystery, known only through the recollections of those who were there. The fire that destroyed the manuscript may have been a tragic event, but it ultimately proved to be a blessing in disguise. The destruction of the first draft allowed Stevenson to create something truly remarkable, and Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde has since become a classic of Gothic horror literature, continuing to captivate readers to this day. articles.title: Sydney Sweeney and Jenna Ortega Wear Elias Matso's Twisted Corsets on Red Carpet
articles.summary: Elias Matso's corsetry creations are inspired by iconic designers like Charles James and Bob Mackie.
articles.content: Elias Matso's work as a twisted corsetier has been making waves in the fashion world, with high-profile clients like Sydney Sweeney and Jenna Ortega turning heads on the red carpet. Growing up, Matso was captivated by the art of costume design after watching Julie Andrews in Victor/Victoria - her elaborate outfits left an indelible mark on his young mind. Matso's fascination with extravagant costumes has clearly influenced his own approach to fashion, evident in his avant-garde and couture corsetry creations. His style is inspired by iconic designers like Charles James, Bob Mackie, Mugler, and Mr. Pearl. A recent graduate of Polimoda in Florence, Matso's designs often feature intricate details and dramatic flair - much like the Art Deco gowns and decadent headpieces that initially sparked his interest in costume design. Designers often look back on their childhood experiences for inspiration, but for Elias Matso, his early years were marked by a desire to create and manipulate the world around him through paper dolls. As he fashioned clothes for his paper self, Matso was developing an essential skill - the ability to imagine and bring ideas to life. This talent would serve him well in his future endeavors as a designer. Matso's third year of design school was pivotal, as it allowed him to explore themes that resonated deeply with his own experiences. He wanted to capture the tension that children often feel when growing rapidly and struggling to keep up with their changing bodies. This sense of disconnection is particularly pronounced in the queer community, where individuals may face conflicting expectations around gender identity. Matso's designs reflect this internal conflict, as seen in his literal interpretations of twisted silhouettes. The designer's frustration during his senior year was a far cry from the success he would later achieve. After failing to secure jobs in New York, Matso considered taking up an unconventional career path - scooping ice cream at Van Leeuwen's. The art of creating a perfect fit is a delicate balance between aesthetics and anatomy. In the world of corsetry, every body is unique, responding differently to fabric and structure. This is why fittings are crucial, allowing for adjustments that cater to individual proportions. When things don't go as planned, and garments fail to translate from runway to real life, it's often due to a lack of personal connection during the fitting process. Matso emphasizes the importance of meeting clients in person, which she believes leads to better outcomes. This approach allows her to understand their needs and preferences, tailoring her designs accordingly. The conversation between designer, client, and garment is complex, influenced by both personality and physiology. As Matso notes, people's bodies respond differently to fabric and structure, requiring a nuanced understanding of each individual's unique characteristics. By checking in with clients before, during, and after fittings, she ensures that her designs meet their needs. To spark inspiration for new collections, Matso often delves into the archives of museums like the Whitney or Guggenheim. This process involves surrendering control to the unknown, as one never knows what treasures will be uncovered. For this particular project, a single painting led her to Mark Ranger's website, setting off a chain reaction that would shape the collection. The question remains: where do designers begin when starting a new project? Matso's approach is one of discovery and exploration, rather than deliberate planning or control. By embracing the unknown and allowing herself to be guided by unexpected sources, she creates designs that are both beautiful and functional. Collaboration was key in creating a unique and functional design. The process involved exploring similar themes and techniques to create something entirely new. This approach led to the development of a corset made from steel boning, an unexpected yet effective material. The use of steel boning in corsets is not new, but rather it's a common feature found inside many traditional corsets. Matso had already accumulated a stockpile of this material and decided to repurpose it by cutting it into smaller pieces to create a unique design. In addition to innovative materials, the corset also incorporates crystals from Preciosa, a company that supplies crystals to high-end brands. This collaboration was facilitated through a trip taken by Preciosa's team to Matso's school. The relationship with Preciosa allowed for the incorporation of these beautiful and delicate elements into the design. The focus on craftsmanship in fashion has been waning in recent years. Many designers now prioritize speed and efficiency over traditional techniques, which can result in lower-quality products. This shift is frustrating for artisans who have dedicated their time and skills to creating exceptional pieces. Despite the emphasis on mass production, there are still those who value handmade items and appreciate the effort that goes into crafting each piece. For Matso, this appreciation is not just about aesthetics but also about the longevity of a product. A well-made item will stand the test of time, whereas its cheaper counterparts may falter. The undervaluing of skilled artisans in fashion is a pressing issue for many emerging designers. With technology and social media making it easy to fake or manipulate images and information, authenticity becomes increasingly important. The value of handmade items lies not just in their appearance but also in the quality and craftsmanship that goes into creating them. The relentless pace of modern manufacturing can be overwhelming, forcing many to sacrifice quality and craftsmanship in favor of speed. Craftsmanship is a rare commodity these days, and it shows in the attention to detail that goes into creating each piece. As Elias Matso's brand continues to grow, he faces the daunting task of balancing his artistic vision with the financial realities of running a business. Every day brings a new request for free or low-cost work, leaving Matso wondering if he can maintain his standards in the face of mounting pressure. It's not just clients who are asking for favors, often it's intermediaries or agents who seem to have no qualms about making unreasonable demands on emerging designers like Matso. As a stylist, Elias Matso values the importance of building one-on-one relationships and engaging in meaningful conversations with his clients before dressing them. These personal connections allow him to tailor his approach to each individual's unique needs and preferences, resulting in more effective styling outcomes. Matso is currently working on a new project with actress Laverne Cox, an opportunity he has long been eager to pursue due to her appreciation for the intricacies of the creative process. Laverne Cox herself has expressed admiration for Matso's attention to detail and dedication to bringing his vision to life, qualities that she believes make him an exceptional stylist. articles.title: Supreme Court to Rule on Trump Asylum Ban Policy
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has agreed to rule on a key aspect of President Donald Trump's immigration agenda: whether his administration can ban asylum claims at the southern border.
articles.content: The Supreme Court has agreed to rule on a key aspect of President Donald Trump's immigration agenda: whether his administration can ban asylum claims at the southern border. A federal judge previously ruled that the policy enacted by Trump on the first day of his second term was unlawful, but it remains in effect while litigation continues. This decision is now headed for the highest court in the land, where a ruling is expected before the end of June. The Supreme Court's verdict will be the final say on a contentious issue that pits presidential power against federal law enacted by Congress, which outlines procedures for asylum claims at the border. The Trump administration has asserted broad authority over immigration decisions, sparking debate about its limits. In making its decision, the court will consider the implications of Trump's proclamation issued January 20, 2025, in which he declared an "invasion on the southern border. This declaration has led to a ban on asylum claims for those who cross the border without required paperwork. The case is part of a series of significant immigration-related disputes that the Supreme Court is currently considering, including other Trump administration policies. The Trump administration's asylum ban is facing another hurdle as it heads to the Supreme Court for a final decision. At stake are the powers of the President under federal immigration laws and the Constitution. According to Solicitor General Noel Francisco, the policy falls within the scope of these powers. The administration argues that the ban rests on a commonsense understanding of the President's inherent and delegated powers to exclude aliens, as written by Francisco in court documents. The plaintiffs, including 13 unnamed individuals and three immigration groups, disagree with this assessment. Their lawyers at the American Civil Liberties Union claim that the policy undermines asylum rules established by Congress. The INA sets out a process under which immigrants can argue they have credible fear of torture or persecution if returned to their home country. The ACLU argues that the president cannot simply create a new removal system that disregards these protections. In court papers, they assert that the president may not invent by fiat a new removal system that eviscerates the protections Congress mandated by statute. The lower courts have already ruled against the administration on this issue. District Judge Randolph Moss and the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals both upheld the ban's challengers. The administration's decision to seek Supreme Court review suggests it is determined to settle the matter once and for all. The Supreme Court is set to rule on another key immigration case involving President Trump's asylum ban, amidst a string of high-profile decisions on border control and deportation procedures. This latest case involves the administration's practice of deporting immigrants to third countries" they have little or no connection with, if they cannot be sent back to their home nations. The justices will consider the implications of this policy, which marks a significant departure from previous approaches to handling immigration cases. The Supreme Court has already made several notable rulings on Trump's immigration policies, including upholding his travel ban targeting mostly Muslim-majority countries and blocking his executive order seeking to limit birthright citizenship. In a separate case, the court will examine the administration's decision to detain indefinitely thousands of people in deportation proceedings, a shift from previous practices that released immigrants while their cases were being adjudicated.
